subject: baseball pitcher
title: A Chimp Is Twice as Strong as You, but It Can't Throw Past 20 MPH

scenes.text: A chimp is twice as strong as you. It can barely throw.
Pound for pound, that is. But a chimpanzee's best throw is only around 20 miles an hour.
The secret is the shoulder. Cock your arm back and its tendons and ligaments stretch like a slingshot.
Then they snap forward. The upper arm spins at 9,000 degrees a second, the fastest motion the human body makes.
That shoulder appeared two million years ago, about when our ancestors began to hunt. We didn't out-muscle the apes. We out-threw them.

description:
A chimpanzee is about twice as strong as a human, pound for pound, but it can only throw at about 20 miles an hour.
A 2013 study in Nature led by Neil Roach filmed 20 college baseball players with motion-capture cameras and found the difference is in the shoulder: when the arm is cocked back, tendons and ligaments stretch like the rubber band of a slingshot, then release, spinning the upper arm at up to 9,000 degrees per second, the fastest motion the human body produces. Bracing the players' shoulders cut their throwing speed by 8 percent on average. The low, wide shoulders, flexible waist and twisted upper-arm bone that make this possible came together in Homo erectus about 2 million years ago, around the earliest signs of effective hunting.
How fast do you think you can throw? Comment below.
first_comment: With braces limiting their shoulders, the pitchers in the study lost 8 percent of their speed. What can humans do that no other animal can?
